name: Crooked Fingers
label: Merge
lede: Eric Bachmann walked out of the noise of Archers of Loaf and into a band named for his grandfather's CB-radio handle, then wrote slow, dark songs from a Seattle cargo van, between sandwich orders in Denver and from a classroom in Taipei.

eras.title: Out of the Archers' wreckage
eras.text: Archers of Loaf had worn Eric Bachmann out by 1998. He dropped the shouting for a low croon and made Crooked Fingers a home for his songs and whoever was around, first on Athens' WARM label, then at Merge Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Eric Bachmann · Wikipedia: Crooked Fingers
years.h: Archers of Loaf end, and Bachmann starts over under his grandfather's CB handle
years.p: Touring burns out [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]] in late 1998. Eric Bachmann starts Crooked Fingers as a solo project, named for his grandfather's CB radio handle.
years.xp:
Bachmann was born in Greensboro, North Carolina, in 1970 and began as a saxophone major at Appalachian State. Between Archers records he had already made instrumental albums as Barry Black, with help from [[Ben Folds|51b7f46f-6c0f-46f2-9496-08c9ec2624d4]] among others.

Crooked Fingers was never a fixed lineup. Bachmann was the only constant, and the players changed from record to record.

years.p: The debut comes out on Athens, Georgia's WARM Records. The Archers noise is gone; the songs are slow, acoustic and sung low.

years.h: Bring On the Snakes is the last WARM record
years.p: The second album closes out Crooked Fingers' time on WARM before Eric Bachmann signs with Merge Records.

years.h: Neil Diamond and Queen on the Merge debut
years.p: Reservoir Songs, a covers EP, is the first Crooked Fingers release for Merge. Eric Bachmann takes on songs by Neil Diamond and Queen.

years.h: Red Devil Dawn, first full-length for Merge
years.p: It follows the Reservoir Songs EP, and Merge stays Bachmann's label for most of the band's run.

eras.title: A van in Ballard, a cart in Denver
eras.text: The best-reviewed Crooked Fingers record arrived just as the money ran out. Eric Bachmann answered by moving into a cargo van, then to Colorado, then behind a sandwich cart, and finally into releasing his next album himself.

years.h: Dignity and Shame opens with a song named for a killer bull
years.p: Co-produced with Seattle's Martin Feveyear, the record opens with Islero, named for the bull that killed Spanish matador Manolete. Sleep All Summer outlived it.
years.xp: Sleep All Summer took on a life of its own. [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]] covered it with [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] for a Merge compilation, and [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] recorded it for Hell-On in 2018 with Eric Bachmann singing along.

years.cap: Eric Bachmann and Crooked Fingers at SXSW, Austin, c. 2005
years.h: On the Dignity and Shame tour, the band plays from the middle of the crowd
years.p: Every musician carries an instrument off the stage and plays a few songs among the audience. Former Archers of Loaf bassist [[Matt Gentling|1c821fb5-a3dc-46cf-95da-a0da32004908]] is on bass.

years.h: Bachmann gives up his apartment and lives in a van for eight months
years.p: Broke after a money-losing full-band tour, Eric Bachmann moves into a white 1999 Ford E150 cargo van in Seattle, with a futon in the back and a cassette recorder.
years.xp:
He told Willamette Week he had months of solo touring booked and "didn't feel like paying rent for a place that I was not going to be using." He parked on quiet streets in Crown Hill and Ballard, wrote through the day in Golden Gardens and Discovery Park, and showered at the University District YMCA. A 24-hour Kinko's on Market Street handled the late-night bathroom runs.

He stored most of his things in a storage unit and kept a PO box for an address. A record's worth of songs came out of it in about two months.

years.cap: Eric Bachmann solo at the Horseshoe Tavern, Toronto, September 16, 2006
years.h: The van songs come out as To the Races, under his own name
years.p: Eric Bachmann releases what he wrote in the van as a solo album, not as Crooked Fingers.

years.big: "A great woman... she's the reason I moved there."
q: A great woman... she's the reason I moved there.
years.h: Bachmann moves to Denver and sells Cuban sandwiches from a cart
years.p: Eric Bachmann moves to Colorado for a relationship and spends a summer running the cart for steady money, until touring offers from [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] pull him back on the road.
years.xp: Westword asked about the move. Bachmann didn't name her, but gave the reason plainly.

yt: Eric Bachmann solo, The Grey Eagle, Asheville, December 5, 2009
years.h: Turning down label deals, Crooked Fingers release Forfeit/Fortune themselves
years.p: It comes out through Constant Artists and Red Pig. [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] sings on it, along with [[Silver Jews|1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983]] drummer Brian Kotzur.
years.xp: Mark Nevers and Alex McManus co-produced. Reviews were lukewarm: Pitchfork gave it 5.2.

eras.title: Written in Taipei
eras.text: The last Crooked Fingers album for fifteen years was written half a world away, in the same year Archers of Loaf came back from the dead.

years.h: Archers of Loaf play a surprise show, twelve years after splitting
years.p: Eric Bachmann is back fronting his old band in January 2011.

years.cap: Eric Bachmann with bass and drums at Mountain Stage
years.src: Wikipedia: Breaks in the Armor · Wikipedia: Eric Bachmann
yt: Full show, Johnny Brenda's, Philadelphia, December 10, 2010
years.h: Eric Bachmann writes Breaks in the Armor while teaching in Taipei
years.p: He teaches English in Taiwan, then records in Athens, Georgia, with Liz Durrett, now his wife, singing. It reaches No. 23 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: Liz Durrett is the niece of [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]]. The A.V. Club called these some of the most melodious songs Bachmann had recorded.

eras.title: A sideman, a solo name, a louder old band
eras.text: Crooked Fingers went quiet. Eric Bachmann played guitar behind Neko Case, made a record under his own name, and took Archers of Loaf back into the studio.

years.cap: Eric Bachmann and Liz Durrett of Crooked Fingers with John Vanderslice, Rock and Roll Hotel, Washington DC
years.h: Bachmann spends three years in Neko Case's touring band
years.p: Eric Bachmann plays in [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]]'s band from 2013 to 2016.

years.h: Crooked Fingers retired, album released as Eric Bachmann
years.p: Eric Bachmann puts the band name away and releases an album under his own name.

years.h: After 25 years, Reason in Decline from Archers of Loaf
years.p: Bachmann's energy goes to [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]], and their first full album since the 1990s lands in October 2022.

eras.title: Heavy enough to need a band
eras.text: Merge's reissues of the old records nudged Eric Bachmann back to the name. The new songs were too loud and too full of death to be a solo album.

years.cap: Eric Bachmann, 2025, as Crooked Fingers returns
q: It was heavy, and it made me wish that I had a band.
yt: Crate Digging with Eric Bachmann, Merge Records
years.h: Eric Bachmann brings Crooked Fingers back because the songs wouldn't fit a solo record
years.p: The new songs were too heavy to sound like a solo album, so Bachmann revived the band name.
years.xp:
Why this name and not his own? "It could have been my name, but I feel like it was more collaborative," he told Sun 13.

The songs came while he was dealing with getting older and with several deaths in his family. Bachmann said he didn't intend to write about death; "it's just that's what was there."

years.cap: Swet Deth, Merge, 2026. Artwork by Eric Bachmann's son
years.h: Swet Deth, the first Crooked Fingers album in 15 years
years.p: Merge releases it with guests [[Sharon Van Etten|5a2e9cd3-010a-4aae-9f83-629253284202]], [[Matt Berninger|991813f5-27c6-4ff3-88dd-90e750dad545]] of [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]] and Merge co-founder [[Mac McCaughan|8841967d-3914-4ab9-aca6-94781aa35288]], who sings on the single Cold Waves.
years.xp:
Bachmann's son made the cover art. Liz Durrett sings on the record too, including on Hospital.

Bachmann told Sun 13 he had a heart attack in October (Halloween), with a complete blockage in his right coronary artery, and that natural bypasses from years of conditioning "saved my heart."
